# Continual-ARC task-aee3875c: fill aligned gaps

## Reusable rule

Across four demonstrations (different background/frame colors), find each row and each column that contains two or more cells of the main marker/frame color. For each such row/column, take the span from its first to its last original marker and change every intervening non-marker cell to **2**. Keep all original marker cells unchanged, and do not extend past the extreme markers. Leave cells on rows/columns with fewer than two markers unchanged. Background cells remain unchanged. This applies to internal alignments as well as the large rectangular outline.

Equivalently: draw the horizontal and vertical straight segments connecting aligned same-color marker pixels; color only the gaps along those segments with 2. The marker/frame color is preserved. In the demos the output color for gap-filling is always 2.

## Evidence from demos

- Demo 1: color 3 on background 7; gaps between aligned pixels were filled with 2, including vertical segments and gaps in a bottom horizontal line.
- Demo 2: color 5 on background 7; the missing cell in the top horizontal span and gaps between markers on the right vertical were filled with 2.
- Demo 3: color 9 on background 0; rectangle-edge gaps and other aligned horizontal/vertical marker spans were filled with 2.
- Demo 4: color 9 on background 5; gaps were filled on the rectangle perimeter and on a separate internal vertical alignment, while marker pixels remained 9.

## Solved test instance

The test had background 3, outline/markers 8, and a rectangular frame with corners/extents at rows 0–22, columns 1–19. Complete the gaps on its four sides with 2. There was also an internal vertical alignment at column 8, with markers at rows 2, 7, 12, and 18; fill only the intervening rows (3–6, 8–11, 13–17) in that column with 2. Keep the existing 8s, and rows 23–27 / columns outside the frame at 3. This output was accepted as correct.

## Important distinction

Do not recolor every isolated marker, nor fill the rectangle interior indiscriminately. Only fill cells lying strictly between same-color marker cells on the same row or column. Preserve endpoints and all unrelated cells.
